title: Lena and the Veil Anew
premise: In the city of Corvane, where magic was outlawed after the Veil War, Paloma Blackwood survives by selling harmless charms and hiding his true gift. When the crown's witch-hunters begin executing anyone with the gift, Paloma learns the truth: King Aldric died years ago, and a parasitic entity called the Hollow Crown wears him still, feeding on the city's bound magic. Guided by the last elders of the Blackwood guild, Paloma must gather three shattered keys to unbind the king's soul, while evading the hunt led by his own estranged sister, Serah. In the end, Paloma breaks the Crown in the throne room at terrible cost—his guild's inherited power dies with it—and chooses justice over law by sparing Serah and rebuilding magic openly among the people.
about_author: Wendell Villalobos is a former archivist from the high desert towns of New Mexico who writes fantasy about institutions, inheritance, and quiet rebellion. His short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies; this is his first novel.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He sells a luck-charm to a dockworker, hiding his real gift behind sleight of hand, and we see the poverty and fear of magical folk in outlawed Corvane. Beat: weary routine masking deep loneliness.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Bell Gate
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The crown posts edicts: all gifted persons must register or be hunted. A neighbor boy is taken that same night. Beat: dread arrives; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He digs up his grandmother's cache beneath the old guildhouse and finds her journal describing the Hollow Crown and three keys needed to unbind the king. Beat: reluctant inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: The Last Elder
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He seeks Maren Ostwick, the final living elder, now disguised as a laundress. She confirms the king is dead and tests Paloma's gift painfully. Beat: fear tempered by purpose.

chapters.title: Serah in Grey
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Revealed as the hunt's chief investigator, she interrogates a charm-seller and suppresses doubt about her orders. Flashbacks show her break with Paloma over their grandmother's 'madness.' Beat: cold duty cracking.

chapters.title: The First Key: Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He retrieves the salt key from a drowned chapel in the harbor, nearly caught by hunters, saved by an unlikely ally: Tovan, a disgraced hunter. Beat: terror and first trust.

chapters.title: Registers and Ash
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. She burns the registry of registered gifted citizens to protect them, a secret act of sabotage. Beat: justice begins to outweigh law.

chapters.title: The Guild That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Maren reveals the Blackwood guild once served the crown itself—and helped bind the king when he begged for death. Beat: shame of inheritance; heroes were complicit.

chapters.title: The Second Key: Iron
chapters.summary: Tovan's POV. He leads Paloma into the hunter citadel's vaults to steal the iron key, betraying his order. They are seen escaping. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Ordered to find the vault thieves, she recognizes her brother's signature charm-work at the scene. Beat: devastating recognition; loyalty torn in two.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Laundress Row
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Serah corners Paloma; Maren intervenes and is fatally wounded covering their escape. Dying, Maren names the third key's location: inside the palace itself. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Disguised as a clerk, Paloma enters the palace and witnesses the court: nobles hollow-eyed, smiling too long, the king motionless on his throne. Beat: horror of corrupted power made visible.

chapters.title: The Third Key: Bone
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The bone key is the king's own fingerbone, kept in the royal reliquary. Paloma steals it during a state banquet, brushing past the thing wearing Aldric's face—which looks directly at him. Beat: it knows.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: The Crown's POV (unusual chapter). It offers Paloma power, safety, even Serah's protection if he abandons the unbinding. Beat: temptation articulated; corruption shown as seduction, not force.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He refuses and flees the city walls with Tovan, wounded. In hiding, he studies the binding rite and learns its price: the caster's inherited gift will be consumed entirely. Beat: acceptance of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Serah's Choice
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. She discovers the Crown ordered the hunts not to find mages but to harvest them. She defects, bringing evidence and the citadel's secret tunnels. Beat: reconciliation begun through shared cause.

chapters.title: The People's Quiet Army
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. Charm-sellers, laundresses, dockworkers—the invisible gifted—organize to hold the streets while Paloma ascends. Beat: hope as collective action, not lone heroism.

chapters.title: Storming the Veil
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The assault on the palace begins; Tovan falls holding the gate. Paloma reaches the throne room as the Crown unleashes harvested magic against the crowd below. Beat: climax ignites; cost already paid.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With Serah shielding him, he performs the rite with all three keys. The Crown fights with memories and lies; Paloma answers with his grandmother's journal read aloud. Beat: climax peak—truth versus possession.

chapters.title: The Gift Spent
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Crown shatters; King Aldric's soul is freed and dies at peace. Paloma's inherited gift burns away completely—he is ordinary, empty, alive. Beat: victory laced with loss.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. She refuses to arrest Paloma, publicly resigns, and testifies about the Crown before a stunned council. The old laws against magic collapse under the revelation. Beat: accountability without vengeance.

chapters.title: Lena and the Veil Anew
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, one year later. Magic returns openly; the guild reopens its doors teaching freely rather than hoarding. Paloma, giftless, becomes its first non-magical teacher. Beat: resolution—inheritance redefined as what we pass on, not what we possess.
